children: Exxonmobil Holdings Corporation (NYSE:XOM) reported robust Q2 results—$14.5B net income, $17.2B FCF and strong upstream profit—while raising LNG and free-cash-flow guidance, accelerating Guyana recoveries and FPSO buildout, and launching bond repurchase offers as Brent climbed to $105.
XOM Q2 Net Income, FCF Rise

: XOM posted Q2 net income $14.5B and free cash flow $17.2B; upstream profit $7.93B. Brent rose ~4% to $105.26. Stock peaked $167.67, later ~$164.01. FCF yield ~9%; price ~28.8% above GF Value $127.35.
: ExxonMobil (XOM) accelerated Guyana cost recovery by ~$55B, launched a fifth FPSO, plans a ninth vessel, expects higher free cash flow 2025–2030 and slight entitled volume cuts from Q3.
XOM LNG Demand Outlook, Targets Raised
: ExxonMobil (XOM) forecasts LNG demand rising from ~400 MT to 500 MT by 2030 and 1,000 MT by 2050. Company raised its LNG sales target to ~50 MT/yr by 2030, from 40 MT.
: ExxonMobil (XOM) via subsidiary Pioneer is offering cash tenders to repurchase 1.900% notes due 2030 and 2.150% notes due 2031. Offers expire Sept 14, 2026; settlement expected Sept 16, 2026.
